Building the ultimate command center for your smart home is actually quite simple: grab an old iPad, mount it in a prominent spot in your home, and let it do one thing. The excellent Apple Home app, Dashboard for your home, solves this perfectly. Cameras, thermostats, lights, local weather, and your calendar — all on a single screen.

HomeKit Weekly is a column series dedicated to smart home accessories, automation tips, and Apple's smart home framework.

For me, camera support is the best feature. You can preview up to four Apple Home cameras simultaneously in live view, and upgrading to Premium unlocks unlimited cameras; there's also a one-tap live button that instantly switches all feeds to live streaming. Tap any camera to view it full-screen. If your camera supports two-way audio, that functionality is built right in as well.

For home management, you can control up to four thermostats and eight switches — such as lights, outlets, and fans — and group them by room. The app also pulls a six-day forecast for your home's location.

The calendar view is a thoughtful addition that makes this app more than just a smart home management tool. It displays a weekly overview of shared calendars, highlights the next event, and lets you swipe left or right to switch between weeks. If you have multiple calendars, such as sports schedules, you can even set custom text colors for each one — very practical indeed.

What can Dashboard for your home do?

When the iPad is idle, the app automatically goes to sleep and can be woken up with a tap, the front camera, or HomeKit motion sensors. It also automatically follows light or dark mode based on your iPad's settings.

The latest version of the app has also added 3D floor plans. You can upload an image of your home's layout, and the app will render it into a bird's-eye view, with lights, blinds, sensors, and door locks marked as tappable icons in their actual positions within rooms. For example, if you want to turn the living room lights on or off, just tap the light bulb icon in the living room.

Below the floor plan, real-time camera thumbnails for entryways and outdoor spaces each have their own live indicators. Even without leaving the app's main screen, you can keep an eye on the front door or backyard at any time. On the right side of the app, there are quick scene buttons, positioned right below the status bar confirming all windows and gates are closed.

The weather info card displays the current temperature along with a six-day forecast; the per-room temperature cards just below let you view and manage each thermostat independently. The calendar panel shows upcoming events for up to seven days, with a countdown timer counting down in days, hours, minutes, and seconds to important dates like holidays or birthdays.

iCloud backup of settings has now also been added, so if you use the app across multiple iPads, you can easily import and export your settings.

The app itself is free, and the Premium tier — which costs US$9.99 per year — unlocks unlimited cameras and thermostats, and also includes the floor plan feature. The developer has also stated that the app does not collect any data.

Conclusion

If you have a spare iPad and you're into Apple Home, this is absolutely a great way to put it to good use. It works even better paired with this wall mount. The app requires iPadOS 17 or later, as well as an existing HomeKit setup. If you just want to try it out, running it on an iPhone in portrait mode with a scrollable layout works perfectly fine too.

Dashboard for your home is now available for free on the App Store.
